key_insight: Asymmetric contrastive pre-training can transfer longitudinal EHR representations across countries by clustering patients with the same positive outcome without forcing negative cases together.
clinical_relevance: This could improve few-shot prediction and cross-site model portability when local labeled data are limited, especially for incident disease tasks.
method: Pre-trained temporal Transformer encoders on 3.98 million patients from Taiwan’s NHIRD.
Used Asymmetric Supervised Contrastive Learning to emphasize shared target outcomes while avoiding over-clustering negatives.
Applied a hybrid semantic mapping pipeline to align clinical vocabularies and transferred models to MIMIC-IV and EHRSHOT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved transfer over random initialization on MIMIC-IV, strong few-shot performance on EHRSHOT, and higher mean AUPRC than BCE transfer on all four tasks and Standard SupCon on three of four in a matched-scale ablation.
watch_item: Cross-national transfer still depends on vocabulary mapping quality and may not generalize equally well across tasks, with a small AUPRC drop on readmission versus Standard SupCon.
paper_title: Bridging the EHR Divide: Asymmetric Contrastive Learning for Cross-National Medical Representation Transfer
